routeSelection.basis: OER Article 10.2 names three specialisations (Philosophy, Politics, Economics) and Article 11.4 requires every student to follow exactly two of them; the normalized target is the generic bachelor and names no specific pair. All three pairings share an identical60ECofYear1common units plus12ECof sharedYear2Practice and an identical Year-3 structure, and combine exactly two disciplines to the same depth (two compulsory courses per chosen specialisation plus four restricted electives, at least one per chosen track), so no pairing is more representative of the programme's broad academic identity, and none is less specialised, than another under the curriculum page, future page or OER Article 10.1's own symmetric description of the three disciplines. The OER's Appendix 1 (Programme overview) prints exactly three annual-plan tables in a fixed order -- 'TRACKS PHILOSOPHY & ECONOMICS', then 'TRACKS PHILOSOPHY & POLITICAL SCIENCE', then 'TRACKS POLITICAL SCIENCE & ECONOMICS' -- so the official-order tie-break selects the first-listed pairing, Philosophy & Economics, fixed before any UCR course was considered and independent of UCR fit.

core: PPE's integrated multidisciplinary identity: examining complex societal problems through combined philosophy, political-science and economics perspectives
Evaluating and constructing solutions to urgent societal challenges using multiple disciplinary lenses together
Ethical reasoning applied to public policy and social choices, and the history of philosophical ideas grounding it
Political science foundations shared by every PPE student regardless of chosen tracks: the state, power, political conflict, and comparative political systems
Microeconomic and macroeconomic foundations shared by every PPE student, and how markets, wellbeing and public choice interact

Philosophy track: compulsory philosophy of science and political philosophy, with restricted ethics/history/global-justice choices; epistemology is an available elective, not selected in this illustration
Economics as a formal Year-2 specialisation: micro/macro-economic methods and policy, behavioural, public and international-trade economics
Formal mathematical, statistical and logical methods -- including decision theory and rigorous argument -- trained across the Methods of PPE sequence
Independent PPE research culminating in a bachelor thesis, within one discipline or across disciplines as appropriate.
Combining two of PPE's three disciplines in structural depth, as VU's own Year-2 specialisation requires of every student
adjacent: Political institutions, international relations, governance and applied policy as a Politics direction, combined with another PPE discipline
Philosophy and Political Science as the second official pairing: ethical agency, authority, rights and political institutions
questions: How should climate change, migration, AI and international development be governed, and what do economics, political institutions and ethics each contribute to that policy analysis?

What professional and career directions -- policymaking, political leadership, think-tank and policy consulting, journalism and academic research -- does a combined philosophy-politics-economics training prepare graduates for?

alternatives.label: Philosophy & Economics: Ethics, Markets and Public Choice
alternatives.labelReason: Names the actual disciplinary weight and organising question; specialist VU equivalence and recurring integrated applications are not claimed.
alternatives.concept: Study ethical agency, emotion and responsibility alongside economic models of markets, public policy and decision-making. Five philosophy courses and six economics courses form the core. Political philosophy, comparative politics, public policy analysis and quantitative and qualitative research support that combination.
progression: The workbook confirms all 24 placements and earlier gateway prerequisites, Year-1 Personal & Professional Development and at least six 300-level courses. Foundations precede advanced work where available.

alternatives.label: Political Economy & Global Governance
alternatives.labelReason: Names the actual disciplinary weight and organising question; specialist VU equivalence and recurring integrated applications are not claimed.
alternatives.concept: Study how political institutions shape markets and how economic decisions affect governance. Five politics courses and six economics courses form the core, with international and constitutional law and the history of states and empires. Western philosophy and ethics provide a foundation in the third PPE discipline.
progression: The workbook confirms all 24 placements and earlier gateway prerequisites, Year-1 Personal & Professional Development and at least six 300-level courses. Foundations precede advanced work where available.
alternatives.distinctness: Politics and economics gain weight through international institutions, law and conflict while philosophy remains foundational. Unique courses on each side of each pair: UCR option 1: 9 (67.5 EC).

alternatives.label: Philosophy & Politics: Agency, Rights and Institutions
alternatives.labelReason: Names the actual disciplinary weight and organising question; specialist VU equivalence and recurring integrated applications are not claimed.
alternatives.concept: Study ethical agency, rights and political authority alongside comparative politics, international relations, EU institutions and conflict. Five philosophy courses and five politics courses form the core, with law and qualitative research. Economics is limited to an introductory course.
progression: The workbook confirms all 24 placements and earlier gateway prerequisites, Year-1 Personal & Professional Development and at least six 300-level courses. Foundations precede advanced work where available.
alternatives.distinctness: Advanced philosophy, rights and political institutions take precedence over economics beyond the introductory course. Unique courses on each side of each pair: UCR option 1: 8 (60 EC), UCR option 2: 7 (52.5 EC).

selection.assessment: The three routes follow VU’s evidenced discipline pairings and change curricular weight substantially. The closest option links advanced philosophy and economics to public choice. The political-economy option prioritises international institutions, law and conflict, while the philosophy-and-politics option links agency and rights to political authority and limits economics to an introduction. All exceed the four-course distinctness floor. Generator rows 5102–5111, 5122, 5123 and 5125 are assigned to the closest route or the political-economy candidate. Career and topic examples 5126–5136 do not justify another option.

notes.text: The UCR options offer different combinations of philosophy, politics and economics. VU has a dedicated Philosophy of Science course and an integrated PPE in Practice sequence. Its supervised tutorial leads to a required 12 EC thesis. Optional UCR independent research is outside the scheduled 180 EC.

audience.programmeDescription: VU’s Philosophy, Politics and Economics degree examines social questions through philosophical argument, political analysis and economics. Students begin with all three disciplines, specialise in two and apply their learning in a sequence of interdisciplinary courses. A supervised tutorial prepares them for the required individual thesis.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR offers three ways to combine these fields: philosophy and economics, political economy and global governance, or philosophy and politics. VU adds a dedicated sequence of interdisciplinary applications, specialist coursework and a compulsory supervised thesis.

curriculum.limitation: This 180 EC route shows one permitted combination of four second-year electives, qualitative research methods and a 30 EC study-abroad package. VU approves the courses taken abroad. Students complete the required earlier credits before starting the tutorial and thesis.
